reviews.text: A rewatch of a teenage classic, just for easy watching. The Simpsons Movie holds up, for me. The first half has some solid laughs sprayed throughout it, whilst the second half does less funny stuff, but feels a tad more emotionally impactful than you would expect. The problem being that it is all entirely ephemeral. Surprised its taken so long for a sequel, as think this actually handles the step-up from series to film quite well. Didn't feel much of a pacing problem. Might be nostalgia earning it an extra half star though.

The movie manages to preserve the spirit of the series, with its irreverent humor, social and political satire, and that wonderfully absurd quality that has made the Simpson family a pop-culture icon. Homer is, naturally, at the heart of it all, and his perfect combination of stupidity, selfishness, and genuine love for his family still works brilliantly. It may not offer anything particularly groundbreaking compared to the series, and because it stays so faithful to its original style, at times it feels like watching a very long episode. But that's also its greatest strength: it never tries to become something The Simpsons isn't. Funny, irreverent, and packed with memorable moments. It may not be the deepest or most innovative animated movie out there, but for a Simpsons fan, it's almost impossible not to have a great time watching it.

En toda relación llega un momento en el que dice: "Necesito que hagas esto conmigo"... Y sólo hay una repuesta cuando alguien dice eso. Me hace reír bastante. No será una obra maestra y se le nota un poco la dificultad de pasar de un episodio de 20 minutos a una película con el triple de su duración habitual. Pese a que no llega al nivel de sus mejores capítulos, tiene muchos momentos icónicos que sin duda te harán reír y uno que otro momento lindo entre Homero y Marge . ​Tampoco es que sea muy profunda; el antagonista es olvidable y hay muchas cosas que se resuelven en un abrir y cerrar de ojos, pero bueno, supongo que no se le puede exigir demasiada profundidad a la familia amarilla (aunque la serie original sí tiene episodios que lo logran muy bien). ​Me resulta un poco molesto que nos muestre a uno de los Homeros más imbéciles y egoístas por momentos (y eso ya es mucho decir), aunque por suerte se redime después de estropear la mayoría de las cosas.

While on the surface, this film feels like a continuation of the extremely long running beloved animated series, it really is a deeply complex insight into the world of a (almost) nuclear family on the brink of destruction due to an emotionally absent father. When considering that this movie came out in 2007 at the height of the 5th Harry Potter film, Spider-Man 3, and the newest Pirates of the Caribbean, this movie, often flies under the radar for being one of the most insightful movies of the year. However, this doesn’t mean that its impact is any less important. While, it didn’t break any records in the box office it’s still manages to give an extremely nuanced view at the detriment behind what will occur when somebody chooses themselves over their loved ones. Homer in this showcases his duality by stepping into the antagonist role by being a character that just can’t seems to stop screwing up. As a result of this, he ends up, turning his entire family and friends against him and as audience members we get to watch him deal with the isolation involved with destroying the structured comfortability associated with familial ties. This is an extremely refreshing take on the series since often cheap jokes are written off to excuse Homer for his genuinely awful behavior. This movie does something smart by allowing the audience to see how Homer’s actions towards his family create turmoil to the point of Marge literally stealing the kids to take them away from the situation Homer has caused. This film is not only a masterclass in the human condition, but it also showcases how regardless of how terrible of a person homer is he still like every human deserves forgiveness. It’s sort of a beautiful story wrapped up in a 90 minute runtime that had me laughing as hard as I did the first time I watched it. Also, it has spider pig and he’s awesome.

I think one of the reasons this works so well for me is the timelessness of the comedy, you could put this movie in theaters today and change nothing and it'd still be a hit, something that can't be said for many many comedies. Besides aging wonderfully comedically, the story here is exactly what I personally love for theatrical TV movies. There's a plot that warrants a longer runtime yet still space for small bits and antics that make it feel like I'm still watching an episode. This might sound insane but I really cannot stand it when a TV show gets a theatrical release and it feels like I'm watching TV characters in a movie not  a longer higher budget episode. Examples of ones I like are this obviously, the Bob's Burgers movie, Mask of the Phantasm, Cowboy Bebop and ofc like the Demon Slayer, JJK, AOT movies, versus things like the Fullmetal Alchemist movies that feel like transplanted characters in a plot and lowkey detracts from the overall narrative. Anyways off that tangent I really really wish they stuck with emotional beat of Marge leaving Homer a little bit longer, because as thousands of people have said that's by far the strongest moment of the whole film. The animation was something I appreciated as well, swinging the camera around and using perspective in ways you don't see in episodes. All around I had a great time, I'm sad I got banned from watching the Simpsons and didn't get to watch this growing up

Watched this as a series finale after watching seasons 1-18 of the show. They do a good job of raising the stakes, and most fan-favorite characters get at least one chance to shine. Marge taping over the wedding video and Homer realizing what he's lost to the tune of Close to You is still a fantastic call back to "The Way We Was" from season 2. It's not quite golden age Simpsons, but it's close. Honestly, aside from the slight hiccup in seasons 11 and 12, the show remained pretty consistent the whole way through. Maybe I'll come back to it someday.

As piadas envelheceram incrivelmente bem e continuam fazendo rir do início ao fim, sem perder o fôlego. A abertura já diz tudo: o Homer quebrando a quarta parede e tirando sarro de todo mundo que pagou ingresso no cinema para ver o que passava de graça na TV é simplesmente genial. A atmosfera de ver isso no lançamento deve ter sido uma experiência única. Entre o domo cobrindo a cidade, o clássico Porco-Aranha e o Homer sendo o desastre ambulante de sempre, o filme entrega exatamente tudo o que os fãs queriam, mantendo um ritmo dinâmico, ágil e muito engraçado. Um clássico que não cansa nunca.

The Simpsons Movie is one of those movies I can’t get through without crying, which still feels insane to say about The Simpsons. Homer and Marge’s relationship gives the movie so much more emotional weight than I ever expect, and “Close to You” as their song is genuinely beautiful. That whole side of the movie hits me every single time. It’s still hilarious, still packed with classic Simpsons stupidity, but it also became one of the first animated movies to ever make me genuinely sob. I love this thing way more than I can explain.
